entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Walter of Saint Omer, also known as Walter of Fauquembergues or Walter of Tiberias, was the son of William II of Saint Omer and Melisinde of Picquigny, and prince of Galilee.

A member of the powerful House of Saint Omer, Walter played a key role in the politics of the Crusader states in the late 12th century.

In 1167, Walter participated in the Siege of Acre, a pivotal event in the Third Crusade, and in 1174, he died defending the city against the forces of Saladin.

Walter's legacy is complex, reflecting both the triumphs and tragedies of the Crusader era. His story serves as a reminder of the enduring power of faith, family, and politics in shaping the course of history.

The very mention of Walter of Saint Omer conjures images of dusty tomes, faded frescoes, and crumbling stone walls, testifying to the enduring legacy of a bygone era.
